findings.title: Caching tests deleted without replacement.
findings.body: The whole `Caching` describe block is removed, which deletes the tests for `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` caching. The service still caches both through `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, and the change to Prisma.sql did not make that behaviour obsolete. Nothing now checks it, so a broken cache (for example, `null` filter results being rebuilt on every call, or auth conditions not being cached) would go unnoticed. Port the two tests to compare Prisma.sql values instead of deleting them.

findings.title: Loose public options type removes compile-time checks on scope/teamId.
findings.body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Before, the type was the discriminated union, so `{ scope: "team" }` without a `teamId` did not compile. Now that call compiles. At runtime the zod `safeParse` fails, `this.options` becomes null, and every authorization check returns `1=0`. The caller sees empty insights with no error. Keep `options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions` in the constructor, or make the public type a discriminated union that requires `teamId` when `scope` is "team".

held.title: Public `findMany` removed; callers outside this diff may break.
held.body: `findMany(findManyArgs)` is replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw SQL fragment and no longer merges a caller's `where`, `select`, or other arguments. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, such as the insights tRPC router, will no longer compile. Callers would also have to rewrite their queries as `$queryRaw` and add back any extra `where` filters themselves. I could not see the callers from here. Check that every use was migrated in this PR.
